page.layout: One column of running text, set as two parallel columns of word lists with a running head above; a single printed page, no margin notes; a catchword-free page with a short line at the lower right.
page.notes: The running head reads "AD MITHRIDATEM". The page is a glossary of words in the invented language of Mithridates' vocabulary with their Latin equivalents, two columns, the left in italic. The line "Tibia cum cokend dice." is partly blurred at the right edge; "cokend" is doubtful and may be "concedice" or similar. The word "Love" at the lower right is a catchword-like mark or handwritten addition and is doubtful. No page number is printed. The text at the right edge of the scan is cut off, and some letters in italic words (e.g. "Christiari", "Kangheri", "Kafcht") are uncertain. Left-column words are set in italic and are transcribed without italic markup because the list entries are single lines.
